name: Thomas Baker
description: A representative of the Essex village of Fobbing who, on or around 30 May 1381, told the poll tax commissioner that the village had already paid and would pay no more -- the confrontation that is conventionally treated as the revolt's opening spark. The commissioner's attempt to enforce payment triggered violence in which several officials were killed, after which the unrest spread rapidly through Essex and into Kent.
narrative_function: The named individual at the revolt's very first recorded flashpoint.
